subject: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>, salesops@fintechco.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0600
Subject: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers

Hi Emily / FintechCo team,

Thanks again for co-sponsoring the Chicago webinar last week — we really appreciated the engagement from your team and the live Q&A. I ran a first-pass reconciliation of leads and attribution this morning and I see a ~32% delta between the leads you reported (FintechCo Sales Ops export) and the leads that got routed to your SDR queue in HubSpot. I attached the export you sent and our exported CSV of webinar leads for quick comparison.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm which source/UTM you used on the registration page that should map to your HubSpot campaign?
- If you can share the Sales Ops export with timestamp/lead owner mapping (or confirm whether your ingest filters out trial signups), that will help isolate the gap.

I'm looping in Sergio and Lauren from field ops to align on how Redwood attributes co-sponsor leads (we mark partner-sourced if partner UTM present + manual partner code). If there's a mapping mismatch we should update both sides so pipeline numbers are consistent for this quarter's commit.

Attachments: chicago-webinar-leads.csv, fintechco-pipeline-export.pdf

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.inference.com

From: Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: salesops@fintechco.com, contracts@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers

Michael —

Thanks for the note. We pulled our Sales Ops export and attached the PDF. Our registration page used campaign=FT-CHGO-DEC and utm_source=redwood-partner. We didn't intentionally filter any signups; however, our ingest has a dedupe rule that drops duplicate emails and another rule that trims out obvious test addresses (e.g., test@, example@).

A couple things we noticed on first pass:
- 14 leads are tagged as "marketing_bounce" in our export; they failed initial enrichment and were not routed to SDR.
- 5 leads came through with company names like "Individual" or left blank — our enrichment pipeline dropped those because they didn't meet firmographic thresholds.

I'm happy to stand up a quick call with Sales Ops to walk through the export. We're sensitive to how leads are counted for the quarter so we want the reconciliation to be accurate.

Emily
Emily Park
Head of Demand, FintechCo
emily.park@fintechco.com
Attachments: fintechco-pipeline-export.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:37:00 -06:00
Subject: Re: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers

Michael / Lauren / Naomi —

I dug into our ingestion rules and here's what I found after comparing the two CSVs:
- Redwood export (attached) shows 184 registrants marked with partner_utm=redwood-partner. Our routing rule is: partner_utm takes precedence over generic campaign tag, and we add partner_code=FINTECHCO when both utm_source=redwood-partner and campaign contains "FT".
- FintechCo export lists 235 entries. Of those, 21 are duplicates (email duplicates across sessions) which our system coalesced into 1 lead per email; that accounts for 20 rows.
- Another 15 had malformed emails (missing domain) and were dropped by our validation step.

Net-net after standardizing dedupe/validation logic we still have a 15-lead discrepancy. I re-ran matching by email + phone and found 10 leads that are present in your export but mapped to a different campaign on our side (they hit the generic "redwood-webinars" campaign because the UTM strip failed due to an extra query param ordering).

I suggest the following next steps:
1) FintechCo to share raw registration export with full query string (not just campaign column).
2) Redwood to provide a sample of the 15 unmatched emails with raw click/registration timestamps (I attached a short sample list).
3) Align on a single dedupe window (we currently use 48 hours; confirm you want 24/48/72).

I can take action items 2 and 3 this week. If we resolve the 15 leads as creditable to FintechCo, I propose we commit a one-week extension to track any post-event MQLs that flow in.

Attachments: redwood-recon-sample.csv

— Sergio

From: Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: salesops@fintechco.com, contracts@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:06:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers

Sergio —

Thanks, that level of detail is helpful. I've asked Sales Ops to pull the raw registration feed with full query strings and session timestamps — they said they can deliver by EOD Wed. On the dedupe window: our default is 72 hours but we can accept 48 hours for fairness on co-sponsored events.

One ask from our side: we saw two redwood-tagged leads that converted to SQLs in your system but aren't in our pipeline export. Can you send the HubSpot Lead IDs for those so we can trace on our side? If those were converted post-event, we want to ensure they count toward our influenced pipeline for Q4.

I'll loop back once Sales Ops drops the export.

Emily

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@fintechco.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 16:21:00 -06:00
Subject: Re: Chicago Fintech webinar — attribution gap & reconciled numbers

Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Sales Ops export arrived this morning and I compared the full query strings. Root cause summary: additional tracking parameter "session_id" was appended by the registration vendor and our UTM parser treats unknown params differently depending on ordering. That produced the 10-campaign-mismatch leads Sergio found. The remaining 5 leads are true invalids (malformed email / enrichment failure).

Resolution and asks:
- Actioned: We standardized parsing to accept common extra params by end-of-day Friday; those 10 will now map to partner_code=FINTECHCO and show up in your HubSpot ingest on a re-run.
- Action for FintechCo: Please re-run the ingest of the attached CSV (chicago-webinar-leads.csv) today with dedupe window = 48 hours and accept vendor-supplied session_id param.
- Ask: Can FintechCo confirm the two HubSpot Lead IDs Emily mentioned so we can mark them as influenced-Redwood in our records?

If accepted, we'll update the joint event report and push the corrected numbers into the Q4 deck. I'll also add a brief retro note on the vendor tracking quirks and recommend we add a lightweight pre-event parsing test to the event playbook.

Thanks — closing loop early next week after your ingest confirmation.

Michael
